findings.heading: Weighting / 調査の重み付け
findings.proposition: English: the survey WEIGHT variable must have no missing values. Japanese renders 'weight variable' as 体重の変数, which means a body-weight (mass) variable.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader takes the DANGER warning to be about a body-weight measurement, which this mortality survey does not even collect, and never checks surv_weight_strata / surv_weight_cluster / surv_weight_cluster_strata for NA. svydesign() then silently produces wrong weighted estimates.

findings.heading: Observation time / 観察期間
findings.proposition: English: the end date is the EARLIEST appropriate departure event within the recall period. Japanese says 最も新しい日付 (the LATEST date), reversing the rule; the in-chunk comment at jp line 280 is flipped the same way against English line 350.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader believes find_end_date() takes the latest of left_date and death_date, so they mis-predict which event closes each person's observation window and cannot reconcile the obstime values the code produces.

findings.heading: Load data / データの読み込み (TIP)
findings.proposition: English: the possible values for each variable are specified in the 'choices' sheet/tab of the Kobo dictionary. Japanese names that sheet "options" instead.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader opens their own Kobo dictionary workbook looking for an 'options' sheet, does not find one (XLSForm names it 'choices'), and cannot locate the value labels or the label::english / label::french columns described in the same sentence.

findings.heading: Alluvial/sankey diagram / 沖積図・サンキーダイアグラム
findings.proposition: English: this one diagram type has numerous other APPLICATIONS (cohorts, any setting with state transitions) beyond mobile populations. Japanese instead says there are numerous other GRAPHS (数多くのグラフがあります) for drawing cohorts and such situations.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader concludes that cohorts and other state-transition settings need some different chart type, rather than understanding that the same alluvial/sankey/parallel-sets diagram shown in the chunk below covers all of them.

findings.heading: Clean data / データの前処理（データクリーニング）
findings.proposition: English: yes/no variables must become TRUE/FALSE because the survey package's PROPORTION functions cannot use them. Japanese says the survey package's 人口を扱う関数 (functions that handle population).
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader misidentifies which survey functions impose the constraint, and does not connect the TRUE/FALSE recode to svyciprop() / survey_mean(proportion = TRUE) used later in the Weighted proportions section.

findings.heading: Weighted proportions / 重み付けされた人口比率
findings.proposition: The Japanese adds a parenthetical definition of design effect: 標本の分散の、同じ要素数の単純無作為標本の分散に対する比 (the ratio of the sample variance to the variance of a simple random sample of the same size). The English gives no definition.
findings.reader_consequence: None harmful; the definition is correct. It is content the English text does not carry, so the two language versions no longer state the same thing and the definition is not maintained upstream.

findings.heading: Load data / データの読み込み (CAUTION)
findings.proposition: The Japanese CAUTION states the example dataset is a file named survey_dict.xlsx obtained from the ハンドブックとデータのダウンロード (#data-used) page. The English names no file and no download page, and the adjacent chunk loads the data with appliedepidata::get_data(name = "survey_dict").
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader goes to the download page to fetch survey_dict.xlsx, which is not how the chapter's own code obtains the dictionary, and may conclude the chunk beside the warning is incomplete or broken.

findings.heading: Load data / データの読み込み (TIP)
findings.proposition: The Japanese TIP adds a link to a concrete example dictionary file, MSF-survey-dict.xlsx in the R4EPI/epidict repository. The English TIP contains no such example or link.
findings.reader_consequence: None harmful; the extra example is useful. It is an unshared external reference, so a broken or moved link in the epidict repository will only ever be noticed in the Japanese page.

findings.heading: Observation time / 観察期間
findings.proposition: The Japanese names find_end_date() from sitrep alongside find_start_date(). The English sentence names only find_start_date().
findings.reader_consequence: None harmful; the added function is the one the chunk below actually calls, so the Japanese is the more accurate of the two. The English omission stays uncorrected.
